proposal.utterance: Classify 'Abusus' (the right of abuse, in Roman-law property theory) in BFO terms.

entities.label: Abusus
entities.rationale: Abusus (ius abutendi) is one of the three classical Roman-law incidents of dominium (usus, fructus, abusus). It is the legally recognised power to alienate, consume, or destroy the thing owned. As a legally recognised power inhering in a specific rights-holder by virtue of their property status, it is best typed as a Role (BFO_0000023): it is a specifically dependent continuant whose instantiation is grounded externally in the legal system's recognition of the owner's position, not in any intrinsic physical property of the bearer. It is a subtype of LegalRight (which is already typed as a Role in the working ontology), so rdfs:subClassOf LegalRight is appropriate. It is modelled as a class because 'abusus' denotes a kind of legal incident that can be instantiated by many individual owners.

relations.rationale: Abusus is a specific kind of LegalRight (a Roman-law property incident), and LegalRight is already typed as BFO_0000023 (Role) in the working ontology. Subclassing captures the taxonomic relationship without duplicating the BFO typing.

open_questions: Should Abusus be further distinguished from Usus (right of use) and Fructus (right to fruits) as sibling classes under LegalRight? If so, shall we mint Usus and Fructus as well for completeness?

Is the intended scope purely Roman/civil-law dominium, or should this class also cover analogous common-law powers of alienation? The answer affects whether additional scope annotations (e.g., an 'applies in legal system' relation) are needed.

Abusus in full Roman dominium implies an unconditional power to destroy or alienate; some civilian systems qualify it (e.g., abuse-of-rights doctrine limits it). Should we represent a qualified subtype (e.g., LimitedAbusus) alongside an unrestricted one?
Should an individual instance of Abusus (e.g., the right held by a specific Roman paterfamilias over a specific res) also be added, or is the class declaration sufficient for now?
proposal.rationale_summary: Abusus (ius abutendi) is the Roman-law incident of ownership that gives the dominus the power to alienate, consume, or destroy the res. In BFO terms it is a specifically dependent continuant: it cannot exist without a bearer (the owner) and it inheres in that bearer in virtue of an externally grounded legal relationship (the recognition by the legal system of the owner's status). This makes it a Role (BFO_0000023) rather than a Disposition (which would require internal grounding) or a Quality (which is a measurable property rather than a deontic power). The working ontology already has LegalRight typed as BFO_0000023 (Role/SDC), and Abusus is straightforwardly a species of LegalRight, so it is proposed as a new class that is a subClassOf LegalRight. It is a class (common noun denoting a kind) rather than an individual, because many distinct owners can each bear an instance of Abusus over their respective property.
